correctness.rationale: For H=I−Δ on any finite connected compact Kirchhoff metric graph, the vertex covariance heat trace F(s)=Σ_j (φ_j|V)^T Q(φ_j|V)e^{−sμ_j} is the Laplace transform of a positive measure because Q is PSD. Zero-length paths in the metric-graph heat kernel yield F(s)=S e^(−s)/sqrt(πs)+exponentially small error, S=Σ_v Q_vv/deg(v)>0 (a nonzero PSD Q has positive diagonal). Karamata gives cumulative weighted spectral mass N_Q(Λ)∼2S sqrtΛ/π. Itô isometry then yields critical expected H^(1/4) energy S/(2π) logΛ, supercritical energy S/[π(4α−1)] Λ^(2α−1/2), and subcritical finite energy for all α<1/4. Gaussian zero-one law plus Fernique excludes a.s. membership when mean-square norm diverges. Integrating F(2s) yields small-time S/2 erf(sqrt(2t))+O(exp(−c/t)). Offdiagonal Q only affects positive-length walks to leading small-time order. Independent interval example with Q=[[2,1],[1,3]] gave log-slope 0.7957175 vs target 5/(2π)=0.7957747, corroboration not proof.
risk: Fixed t>0 Gaussian spectral membership; not a simultaneous-all-times or pathwise endpoint statement. Nonzero PSD finite vertex covariance, no nonlinear/potential/nonstandard coupling assumptions.

A prior Resultary paper gives a sharp critical coefficient only on an equilateral star with scalar noise at its center; the present claim covers every compact finite Kirchhoff metric graph and every fixed nonzero correlated PSD vertex covariance, including exact a.s. endpoint exclusion, universal degree-weighted critical and supercritical coefficients, and small-time stochastic energy. value.rationale: The same physically natural noise problem was previously known to lie in subcritical fractional spaces and to fail at a critical index in a highly symmetric star. The reviewed theorem solves the sharp endpoint and exact universal ultraviolet coefficient for arbitrary compact metric graphs and arbitrary correlated rank-deficient vertex covariances, identifying the local degree-weighted invariant S and proving off-diagonal correlations cannot cancel the leading singularity. The general power law and small-time energy give reusable spectral/regularity benchmarks beyond a special case.
risk: Deterministic walk and Weyl laws are prior input; arbitrary equivalent Sobolev norm changes coefficients, and no nonlinear colored-noise extension is claimed.

limitations: Finite compact connected graphs, edge lengths >0, standard Kirchhoff conditions and scalar diffusion; each fixed positive time.
No assertion of path continuity at critical index or extension to white noise on edge interiors.
Potential older equivalence in boundary-noise trace literature explicitly retained.
